chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who has children, and one of his children is absent, and he does not know where he is, and the man dies. So how is the inheritance of the absent one from his father handled? He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is set aside (isolated) until he comes.' I said: 'So, upon his wealth is Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until he comes.' I said: 'So when he comes, does he pay Zakat?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until a year passes over it while it is in his hand.'

key_terms.يُعْزَلُ: It is set aside / isolated (held in reserve)

ai.seo_question: When is Zakat due on the inheritance of an absent heir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific mechanics of Zakat calculation for an absent heir, distinguishing between the period of absence and the period of possession. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that Zakat is tied to the actual holding of wealth (*hawl*) by the owner rather than merely the inheritance event, ensuring fairness in religious obligations during periods of uncertainty.

en.hubeali: Muhammad in Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahimasws about the man who happens to have children for him, so one of his children is absent, and he does not know where he is, and the man dies. So how would one deal with the inheritance of the absentee from his father?’ Heasws said: ‘It would be isolated until he comes over’. I said, ‘So, upon his wealth would be the Zakāt?’ So heasws said: ‘No, until he comes over’. I said, ‘So when he does come over he would purify (pay Zakāt)?’ So heasws said: ‘No, until a year passes by over it, being it in his hand’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has a certain number of children, a certain one of them disappears and he does not know where he is. The man dies. How his legacy is dealt with? He (the Imam) said, ‘His share is kept aside until he comes? I then asked, ‘Is there Zakat on his share?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, until he comes.’ I then asked, ‘Is he required to pay Zakat as soon as he comes?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, until one year passes with the asset in his hands.’”
